steps.explanationAfterStep: Methylamine adds to one aldehyde. Succinaldehyde is symmetrical, so it does not matter which.
Water removes a proton from nitrogen: the neutral hemiaminal. Its nitrogen is now a secondary amine with a lone pair.
A five-membered ring closes fast: the nitrogen adds to the second aldehyde inside the same molecule. Using a 1,4-dialdehyde is what builds the pyrrolidine ring of tropinone.
Water takes the last N–H proton. The 2,5-dihydroxypyrrolidine has a tertiary nitrogen with a free lone pair.
Protonated, the OH can leave as water. The two OH groups are equivalent: either will do.

The nitrogen lone pair pushes out water, giving a cyclic iminium ion. A tertiary nitrogen has no N–H to lose, so the iminium ion stays: it is the electrophile for the first Mannich reaction. The other OH is still there and will become the second iminium ion later.

title: Tropinone: the first iminium ion
subtitle: Methylamine and succinaldehyde close a pyrrolidine ring and make a cyclic iminium ion
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 26 (the Mannich reaction and Robinson's tropinone synthesis)
R. Robinson, A synthesis of tropinone, J. Chem. Soc., Trans., 1917, 111, 762–768

diol.caption: 1-methylpyrrolidine-2,5-diol + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: To make the iminium ion, one OH must leave. Is hydroxide a good leaving group?
Either OH (they are equivalent) takes a proton from H₃O⁺. Two arrows.
OH oxygen lone pair → new O–H bond to the proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond → a lone pair on water's oxygen.
diol.learnerPrompt: Protonate one of the two OH groups.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Protonating the nitrogen gives back an ammonium ion, which cannot push anything out. Protonate an OH so it can leave as water.
Hydroxide is a poor leaving group. Protonate the OH first, so that neutral water leaves.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: the OH takes a proton. Where does the O–H bonding pair of H₃O⁺ go?

iminium.caption: the cyclic iminium ion (a 1-methylpyrrolinium ion carrying an OH) + water

reactants.caption: succinaldehyde + methylamine + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: Amines are good nucleophiles, and aldehydes are good electrophiles. Which atom of an aldehyde is electron-poor?
The nitrogen lone pair forms a new N–C bond to one carbonyl carbon, and that C=O π pair moves onto oxygen. Two arrows.
Nitrogen lone pair → new N–C bond to a carbonyl carbon; that C=O π bond → a lone pair on its oxygen.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Methylamine attacks one of the two aldehydes.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Near pH 7 much of the methylamine is indeed protonated, but a methylammonium ion has no lone pair: it is not a nucleophile. Draw the free amine attacking an aldehyde.
The carbonyl oxygen is electron-rich. The amine attacks the electron-poor carbonyl carbon.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: nitrogen attacks the carbonyl carbon. That carbon now has five bonds: move the C=O π pair.

hemiaminal.caption: hemiaminal + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: The molecule still has a free aldehyde, and its nitrogen still has a lone pair. How far apart are they?
Count round: nitrogen and the second carbonyl carbon would close a five-membered ring. The nitrogen lone pair forms the new N–C bond and the C=O π pair moves onto oxygen. Two arrows.
Nitrogen lone pair → new N–C bond to the carbon of the second aldehyde; that C=O π bond → a lone pair on its oxygen.
hemiaminal.learnerPrompt: The nitrogen, now a secondary amine, closes a five-membered ring onto the second aldehyde.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Protonating the OH and losing water would give an open-chain iminium ion; that route can also reach the ring later. Here the nitrogen still has its lone pair and the second aldehyde is in reach: close the ring first.
The OH could add to the aldehyde and give a cyclic hemiacetal, reversibly. Nitrogen is the better nucleophile, and only the nitrogen ring leads on to the iminium ion.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the nitrogen closes the ring. Now move the C=O π pair of that aldehyde onto oxygen.

zwitterion.caption: zwitterionic adduct + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: The adduct carries O⁻ and N⁺. Which species can give the oxygen a proton?
The oxygen lone pair takes a proton from H₃O⁺. Two arrows.
Alkoxide lone pair → new O–H bond to the proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond → a lone pair on water's oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Protons move through the water, not straight across the molecule. Take one from H₃O⁺.
Losing the amine just reverses the addition. Protonate the alkoxide instead.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: the oxygen takes the proton. Where does that O–H bonding pair of H₃O⁺ go?

protonated-diol.caption: diol protonated on one oxygen + water
hintTiers: Water is now a good leaving group. Which lone pair next door can push it out?
The nitrogen lone pair forms a C=N π bond as the C–O bond breaks. Two arrows.
Nitrogen lone pair → new C=N π bond to the carbon carrying the protonated OH; that C–O bond → a lone pair on the leaving oxygen.
protonated-diol.learnerPrompt: Water leaves, pushed out by the nitrogen lone pair.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Breaking the ring N–C bond would open the ring again. Water is the leaving group, pushed out by the nitrogen lone pair.
Taking the proton off again just reverses the last step. Let water leave.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right: the nitrogen lone pair pushes in. That carbon now has five bonds: let water go.

cyclic-zwitterion.caption: pyrrolidinium alkoxide + H₃O⁺
hintTiers: The ring now carries O⁻ and N⁺, just as after the first addition. Which species gives a proton?
The alkoxide lone pair takes a proton from H₃O⁺. Two arrows.
Alkoxide lone pair → new O–H bond to the proton of H₃O⁺; that O–H bond → a lone pair on water's oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Breaking the new N–C bond just opens the ring again. Protonate the alkoxide.
Protons move through the water, not across the ring. Take one from H₃O⁺.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good. Where does the O–H bonding pair of H₃O⁺ go?

protonated-adduct.caption: adduct protonated on oxygen + water
hintTiers: Which atom carries the positive charge and an acidic proton?
Water takes a proton from nitrogen, and the N–H pair stays on nitrogen as a lone pair. Two arrows.
Water lone pair → new O–H bond to a proton on nitrogen; that N–H bond → a lone pair on nitrogen.
protonated-adduct.learnerPrompt: Water takes a proton from the positive nitrogen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That OH is neutral; taking its proton just undoes the last step. The acidic protons are on the positive nitrogen.
Hydroxide is a poor leaving group, and the nitrogen has no lone pair to push it out yet.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: water takes an N–H proton. Where does the N–H bonding pair go?

protonated-cyclic-adduct.caption: pyrrolidinium diol + water
hintTiers: One acidic proton is left, on the positive nitrogen.
Water takes the N–H proton and the bonding pair stays on nitrogen. Two arrows.
Water lone pair → new O–H bond to the proton on nitrogen; that N–H bond → a lone pair on nitrogen.
protonated-cyclic-adduct.learnerPrompt: Water takes the proton from the positive nitrogen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That OH is neutral; taking its proton undoes the last step. Take the proton from nitrogen.
Hydroxide is a poor leaving group, and the nitrogen has no lone pair yet to push it out.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Good: water takes the N–H proton. Where does the N–H bonding pair go?

mechanismSummary: Methylamine adds to one aldehyde of succinaldehyde; proton transfers through H₃O⁺ and water give a hemiaminal. Its nitrogen then adds to the second aldehyde, closing a five-membered ring, and two more proton transfers give 1-methylpyrrolidine-2,5-diol. Protonating one OH lets the nitrogen lone pair push out water: the cyclic iminium ion, ready for the first Mannich reaction. All these steps are reversible; Robinson ran the reaction in water at room temperature, and Schöpf later showed that buffering near pH 7 gives the best yields.
